Clause (iii)'s content is right in Lean: the bounded quantity is literally F_slow(U^[N]) of (5.24), since stressForce is minus the two radial stress divergences, and the exponent 2Nh-2-M is 2h(N+1)-K_m with K_m = 2h+2+m, independent of N; the axis is included (lo = 0). Clauses (i) and (ii) are each one instantiation away from stated declarations. What is not stated is the quantifier of (5.25): Lean bounds the residual eventually along filters with q -> 0, so the threshold depends on N and m, while the paper asserts the bound at every 0 < q <= 1 and uses that uniformity as Lemma 5.4's hypothesis (5.33). Recovering it needs a compactness and continuity step no declaration states. Hence lean_weaker and DELTA, with A's verdict upheld and B's recovery argument rejected.

findings.summary: (5.25) is asserted at every 0 < q ≤ 1 on a fixed compact profile range; the Lean gives only an eventual bound along filters whose scale tends to 0, so the threshold below which it holds depends on N and m.

No declaration states Proposition 5.3. Its three clauses live in three files: the order-by-order construction in GlobalSlowProfiles, divergence-freeness in AxisymmetricFields/SpatialCurl, and the residual estimate in BaseResidual.
Clause (ii) is stated for the finite sum, but only off the axis, and in a different file from clause (iii) under a different name for the same field. Reaching the axis needs the separate curl route.

The paper's seminorm is the max of mixed space-time partials of order ≤ m; the Lean bounds the full iterated Fréchet derivative norm in the joint variable. The Lean norm dominates every such partial, so this costs nothing.

No declaration states (5.25) for the constructed sequence: finite_error_rate is generic in the coefficients d and profiles f and carries their hypotheses. They are discharged unconditionally for the realized base elsewhere, so the statement is not vacuous.

The paper applies Lemma 5.1 afresh at each order; the Lean Scheme fixes the whole family of near-axis seeds in advance and the recursion repairs only the annulus a ≤ R ≤ b, coupling to the lower orders through the moment rows.
